parsed.why: Trans-specific constitutional and criminal anti-discrimination, gender-identity law, aggravating sentencing, majority public support; no traveler-facing restriction. Weak enforcement, 2017 impunity for murders and 2024 exclusion survey hold it below the acceptance-with-protections tier.

Sodomy statute to 14 years with sporadic enforcement; police documented as a main source of violence against trans people, rape and beatings in the capital, impunity and mob-justice climate. Third-gender traditions and one sanctuary village do not offset state-tolerated targeting.

No criminalisation, court-recognised markers and pride infrastructure, but documented public and institutional discrimination plus physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities, and recent political hate speech with death threats from a leader's supporters.

Public same-sex affection criminalised, documented arrests on false accusations, and mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement amid general impunity and no gender recognition; entrenched stigma and no remedy. State-implicated abuse dominates.

No criminalisation, constitutional equality guarantee, no documented police targeting or trans-specific violence; but guarantee covers orientation only, no gender-identity protection, no recognition procedure, and societal stigma recorded. Thin record extrapolated from non-hostile structures.
